utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would first like to make sure you are receiving interpretation of what is said into your own witness. If so, please say yes. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would be grateful if the interpreters could speak up a little, since I am somewhat deaf.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If the interpreters could speak a little more loudly, that would be useful for the witness. I will ask you my question again. Sir, do you hear -- can you hear what I am saying in your own language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not loud enough. I won't be able to answer the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, the usher should perhaps make sure that the headphones -- that you have put the headphones on correctly. Can you hear me now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I hear you well now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have been called here as a witness for the Defence in order to testify. Before you take the solemn declaration I would like to ask you to tell me your first and last names, your date of birth and your place of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Remzija Siljak. I was born on 15th of November 1953, in the village of Kljaci in Travnik municipality in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What position do you hold at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am retired.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1993, what position did you hold or what rank did you hold, if you were a member of the military.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In 1993, I was first the chief of staff of the 306th Mountain Brigade and then the chief of staff of the Bosanska Krajina OG. And in 1993 in the BH army there were no ranks, but those were the duties I performed, whereas ranks were conferred in 1994 and I was given the rank of major.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Is this the first time you will be testifying in an international court or have you already testified in a national court.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have never testified either -- neither before international court nor before a local court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could you please read the solemn declaration that you will be shown.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You can sit down. Before I give the floor to the Defence counsel who is going to conduct the examination-in-chief, I should like to give you some explanations as to how these proceedings are going to be conducted. This is what I do with every witness so that you know what to expect. You're first going to answer questions which will be asked of you by one of the Defence counsel who is present in the courtroom. After this part of the examination, which is likely to be rather long because you have been scheduled for two days, the Prosecution will also have some questions for you within the framework of the so-called cross-examination. The three Judges that you can see in front of you, pursuant to the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, may also ask any question of you if they deem it appropriate or useful. These issues are regulated. At the same time we are triers of fact and triers of law at the same time because there is no jury in these proceedings. So we will also ask you questions that we deem necessary and useful, depending either on the questions that are going to be asked of you by the parties or because we believe it to be useful and necessary in the interest of justice. We have that right pursuant to the Rules and we will free to ask questions of you. Usually we do not ask many questions. This is the role that is normally played by the parties. We will only have several minutes at the end to ask questions if we deem them necessary. When you answer a question, try to be as clear as possible for the Judges who are in front of you, who have to be able to understand you. If you do not understand the question, feel free to ask that the question be rephrased, especially if the question is too long and if you don't think that you can understand the contents of the question. I should also like to draw your attention to two very important points. You have just read the oath which excludes normally any false testimony. If it turns out that you have lied, you may be subject to charges of perjury. The punishment that is provided for such cases can go to seven years of imprisonment. You're now a witness of the Court. You're no longer a witness of any of the parties. You have to answer the questions, but you're also a witness of the court and a witness of justice and therefore you have a special status. If in the course of your responses you provide answers that might be incriminating, you should be aware of the fact that what you say cannot be used against you at a subsequent date. And for this reason, you have all the more reason to speak the truth. If you feel that there are any difficulties, do not hesitate to inform us of the fact. We are here to deal with any problems that might arise. There are no questions you would like to ask, I will now give the floor to Defence counsel, who will commence with their examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Siljak.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before I proceed with my questions, in addition to what the President of the Chamber has told you, I also have to ask you to bear in mind one additional thing. As you have been informed by the President of this Chamber, it is very important for the Judges of this Chamber to hear everything that you're going to say here. You and I speak the same language. As soon as I ask my question, I know that you are able to start immediately with your answer, but in that case it would be very difficult for the interpreters to convey both my question and your answer. So I have to kindly ask you to pause a little and wait until you hear that the interpretation is finished and then proceed with your answer. Have you understood me?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You have already told us your name, your date, and your place of birth. Could you also tell us, please, what nationality you are and what citizenship you hold.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: I am a Bosniak by nationality and I am a national. I hold citizenship of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where do you currently reside, Mr. Siljak?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: I currently reside in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where did you live at the beginning of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: In April 1992, I lived in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, could you tell us about your education.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: I completed teacher training college.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was your profession or your occupation before the war and where did you work?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: After graduating from teachers' college, I found a job in the village of Visnjevo in Biljanska Valley. And for the first ten years of my life after I graduated, I worked as a teacher in the villages of Biljanska Valley up until 1984.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: After you have had a series of jobs as a teacher, did you do something else? Did you change occupation, and if so what did you do?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Since there was a teachers' college in Travnik, there was always a surplus of teachers. So at one point in time, I became so-called surplus and I applied for a different job, for a job of operations and training chief in my municipality. And I started on that job on the 1st of January, 1984.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you do any military service before the war, and if so in which army?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Yes. I did my military service in the former JNA, that is with the army of the former Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were you given any rank in that army?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: In that army, I was a member of the officers' school in Bileca. Normally one is made lieutenant after that school.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did that have any effect on the fact that you were an admitted member of the Territorial Defence staff in the municipality of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: If I had not completed officers' school and if I had not been a reserve officer, I would have never been able to apply for that job and I would have never been given that position.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You stated that as a teacher you worked in the village of Visnjevo in Biljanska Valley. Can you explain to us what Biljanska Valley is and where that area is located.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: I stated only one village where I worked as a teacher. I also worked in Dub, Cukle, Grahovcici, Han Bila and Kljaci, all of which are situated in Biljanska Valley. That area is part of the Travnik municipality and lies to the north-east of the municipality of Travnik. These villages are part of the valley of the Bila River.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please indicate for us on this map the area in question and after that, if you are familiar enough with the area, I should also like to ask you to indicate the area on the model. There is a pointer on your desk which you can indicate the area on the map, and I think that the usher could also perhaps give you the microphone so that you can continue speaking and providing us with relevant information while you're indicating the area in question. Let me first ask you whether you can recognise this map.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can. But let me just add that as a teacher I was able to really know all of these villages. I am a native from the area, and as an employee of the municipal staff which was involved in planning and preparation of the training of the units of the Territorial Defence staff, I was able to know the entire area of the Travnik municipality because it is in these locations that we carried out our training. So this is how I was able to gain knowledge about the area. I know where these villages are. I am fully familiar with the national composition of the population in this area and I can indicate this on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I should like to ask you now to indicate the area for us on the map so that we and the Chamber have a clear understanding as to the area in question.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: As I have already indicated --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, you have already told us that you can recognise the map. Tell us about the map and tell us how it is that you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: It is a military topographic map. The ratio is 1:25.000. I used this map on a daily basis when working for the Territorial Defence staff for the purpose of preparing the training and making plans and preparations for the training.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you now show us the area of Biljanska Valley and the villages making up that area.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The area I'm going to indicate now is the territory of the Travnik municipality. The municipality of Travnik is made up of two parts. One is the valley of the Lasva River and the other is the village of Bila River. The Biljanska valley, as I have already told you, follows the river of Bila. The Bila River area is not inhabited in the upper part. However, in the lower part of the river, that area is more inhabited and this is where these villages are located, the villages that I have spoken about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please slow down when indicating the area on the map so that we can follow on our screens the area that you are indicating and your words.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: I have stated that the upper part of the valley is not inhabited. The first village is Gluha Bukovica. I did not work in Gluha Bukovica, but I often went there for the purposes of training because there was a TO unit in Gluha Bukovica. The next village located near the Bila River is Visnjevo. In Visnjevo I did work. Actually, this was my first job. Going down the river, we see the village of Dub which is where I worked as a teacher as well. The villages after Dub in Biljanska Valley on the left bank are Orahovo, Zagradje, Skomorje, Bana; and on the right bank, Suhi Dol, Poljanice and Mehurici. The River Bila actually flows through the village of Mehurici, but you cannot see this village on this -- these maps. This village is can be seen on the new map. Then we have the villages of Postinje, Maline. Do you want me to enumerate the villages located on the right bank? They are Postinje, Maline, Guca Gora, Krpeljici. And although those villages are not really in or near the Bila River, they are part of the Biljanska River Valley. Then we have the village of Radoncici, Bandol, Han Bila. The Bila flows through this one. But let me go back to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Miletici, Jezerci, Podovi, Orasac, Cukle, Novo Selo, Piljaci, Brajkovici, Grahovcici. There's also Dolac, Rudnik, and the village of Kljaci on this bank. From Han Bila to the right bank, we see the villages of --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please slow down, Mr. Siljak, so that both the image and interpreters can following your testimony. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: So from Han Bila downstream on the right bank we see the villages Banovici, Rajici, or Zolote, as the population commonly referred to it, Alihodze and Karahodze. And in the lower part of the Bila River we see Pokrajcici on the right bank and on the left bank the villages of Zabilje, Sadovace and Rijeka Bila. And actually the village of Stara Bila where the Bila River joins the Lasva.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On the model - you don't have to repeat all the villages - could you use the model and indicate the general area for us if you are able to recognise it for us on the model as well.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: So there is a valley of the Lasva River --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think the microphone is on.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: As I have indicated, the municipality of Travnik is made up of two valleys: the Lasva valley, starting on the southern slopes of the Vlasic mountain; and the Bila River Valley, which is located to the north-east of the municipality of Travnik and the north-east slopes of the Vlasic mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you're now next to the model, can you please also tell us something about the terrain of the Travnik municipality and Biljanska valley.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Well, you can see for yourself the area. The entire area of the municipality of Travnik is a mountainous area. The largest part of the municipality is occupied by the Vlasic mountain, and on the other side Radalj, Komar, and Moralica [phoen], as far as the Lasva River valley is concerned. As for the Bila River valley, the terrain is similar. The River Bila flows through the mountainous area in the upper part and in the mid-part, and in the lower part the terrain is a bit more even. However, these two areas are separated. You see here that the Lasva River valley is separated from the Bila River valley.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It is separated from a mountain range, right?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You can now go back to your seat. Mr. Siljak, we're just going to dwell upon the Bila River valley for a moment. Can you please tell us what the population is in that valley. Who lived in the Bila River valley?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The Bila river valley was ethnically mixed; however, the majority population was Bosniak and Croat with only two small villages inhabited by Serbs. However, these villages were not really separated. Most of the these -- or rather, many of these villages were mixed and were inhabited by both Croat and Bosniak populations. Likewise, there were cases of villages, Croatian villages, right next to Bosniak villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. I believe you have clarified that. Can we now go back to your position as a member of the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence before the war. Tell me, what was your job in the municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: As I have already indicated, I started on my job as a coordinator for instruction and training, but I was soon transferred to the position of the assistant chief of staff for instruction and training.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this the position that you had when the war broke out? And I apologise if the question is leading. I just need some clarification with respect to the previous question. What was your position at the beginning of April 1992?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: There had been some changes in the meantime in the municipality staff of the Territorial Defence. In peacetime, the assistant chief of staff became assistant commander, and this entailed further changes. And as a result of that in April 1992 my position was assistant commander for instruction and training.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you briefly tell us what is the role of the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence and how it fit in the overall system of the Territorial Defence in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: As part of the armed forces, the Territorial Defence was always tasked with specific assignments linked with the geographical area where it was located. So performing combat assignments in case of attack on the territory of the former Yugoslavia, in particular in the area of the Travnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who were you subordinated to? The municipal staff of the Territorial Defence, who was your superior?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: I think it is important to distinguish between peacetime and wartime staff. The municipal staff of the Territorial Defence as a peacetime organ was a municipal organ of the Travnik municipality, whereas the war staff was a unit which would normally come into existence only in case of war or if it became necessary to defend the country.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the role of the Municipal Assembly with respect to the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: They were in charge of assigning officials to various positions. I, for instance, was appointed by the Municipal Assembly to my position of assistant commander for instruction and training. So the Municipal Assembly was in charge of appointments in various organs, therefore it had a rather important role.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who were members of the units of the Territorial Defence of every Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. municipality, therefore of the municipality of Travnik as well?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The composition of the units, the members of these units were all able-bodied men of the Travnik municipality, regardless of their ethnicity. However -- I don't know if this is necessary, but it might be useful for me to state that the municipal staff was a municipal organ. Horizontally speaking, it was connected to the municipality; however, militarily speaking, the superior command was the district command of the Territorial Defence which was located in Zenica. The municipal staff was in charge of drafting plans for mobilisation of units on the basis of assessment of needs and orders receipt from the superior command and also pursuant to a request issued by the Municipal Assembly for the purposes of providing, for instance, security to important facilities on the territory of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of these units? And also, what was the ethnic composition of the commands of these units and the municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: When I started at the municipality -- at the municipal staff in 1992 and actually throughout that period of time, the ethnic composition of Travnik municipality corresponded to the ethnic composition of the population of the Travnik municipality. In the municipal staff of the Territorial Defence up until 1989 when, pursuant to the law on early retirement of administrative organs, the national composition of the officers of the command and the staff, it was more or less similar to the ethnic composition of the population. However, after that there was no replenishment of the staff. Therefore, the situation was somewhat different at the beginning of the war. There were four Bosniaks in the staff, four Croats, I believe, and three Serbs at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, since when answering my questions you said that everyone from the area of your municipality was mobilised into the unit, tell me about the able-bodied men. In the case of war, where were they mobilised and who was given priority when these men were being mobilised?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: When I started working in the municipality of Travnik, there were two brigades, JNA reserve forces and there was a regiment was replenished with men from the entire area. There were Territorial Defence units. There were police units, units of the military police. There were units of the civilian protection. People who had to do work obligation. There were various bodies that we used for mobilisation. But you asked about priority. Men from the former JNA were given priority, and then manoeuvring units from the TO, and then tactical units from the Territorial Defence. I don't know whether it's necessary to provide further clarifications.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think it's necessary to go into further details. But since that system existed before the war started, we think it might be good for you to provide us with some information about this. I'll ask you some questions about this matter. My first question is: What sort of equipment did the Territorial Defence staff and its units have and who obtained this equipment?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The TO municipal staff, as I said, was in charge of the mobilisation plan for units and it supervised the drafting of plans for developing and supplying Territorial Defence units. And on the basis of these plans, the necessary equipment was obtained. To finance the equipment and the training of the units, one used funds that had -- from the entire population. They would contribute 1 per cent of their salaries, and this would be shared out among the JNA and other structures. And with regard to these funds, the Municipal Assembly would decide about these funds. The Municipal Assembly would be provided with the plan for obtaining funds and the Municipal Assembly would allocate funds for obtaining this equipment, the necessary equipment, and for training units, commands, and Territorial Defence staffs.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, since you worked in the TO staff just before the war, tell me: Was there -- was anything reorganised, were there any changes in the Territorial Defence in a way that might significantly effect subsequent developments in the capacity of your municipality for defence? I'm referring to manpower, equipment.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: I said I started working in the TO staff as of the 1st of January, 1994. When I assumed that post, the TO in Travnik municipality had about 4.200 members. With time, this number diminished. It was reduced to 3 per cent of the population, then to 2 per cent of the population, so that just before the war in 1990 there were about a thousand or even fewer members of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since a minute ago you said that significant funds were allocated from national salaries for the purposes of the Territorial Defence, tell me what sort of equipment, what sort of weapons did the TO have and at the beginning of the war. Was it in a position to make use of its weapons?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The TO units were not units that had heavy artillery, but a TO detachment, a TO battalion that we were composing for the 13th brigade -- TO brigade, other local commune units had weapons in accordance with the establishment. They had infantry weapons -- I'm referring to rifles, light machine-guns, hand-held rocket launchers, anti-armour equipment, recoilless cannons, because this is what the TO units according to the establishment should have had. These weapons were kept in JNA barracks in Muslimeni [as interpreted]. In that barracks, those barracks, the Muslimeni [as interpreted], the Territorial Defence staff built a special warehouse where this equipment was kept. It wasn't possible to keep all the weapons in that one warehouse, but a JNA warehouse also had to be used. When I had only just started working it wasn't a problem to use that equipment for the purposes of training or for other needs. But -- I don't remember the exact date but at some time in 1990 or at the beginning of 1991, there was an order according to which we were no longer to be allowed access to those weapons without special authorisation from a high JNA command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, the Chamber is already aware of the fact that in 1990 there were the multi-party elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Tell me who in the municipality of Travnik won at the elections and how was the government subsequently formed, from the viewpoint of whether these changes had an effect on the organisation of the Territorial Defence staff in Travnik. Could you tell me whether the way in which it was organised was effective as a result of these elections.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The first multi-party elections, the nationalist parties were victorious. And when I refer to the nationalist parties, I mean that the SDA received the greatest number of votes. They were followed by the HDZ and the SDS. This had a significant influence on the appointments of individuals to various positions. So the SDA, since this was a victorious party, was given the position of the chief of the public security station and the position of the TO commander in Travnik. And the HDZ was given the position of the secretary of the secretariat of defence in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, just a while ago --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleagues have informed me and I just checked this -- on page 22, line 12 instead of the word of Slimena being mentioned, which is the name of the JNA barracks, the word Muslimeni appeared. This is something that should be corrected. The name of the barracks is Slimena. As you see here in the JNA barracks in Muslimeni it should say in Slimena. Slimena is the place where those barracks were located. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's continue, Mr. Siljak. You told us about the changes in the structure of the TO staff when power was divided. Tell me at the time who was the commander of the TO staff in which you worked and you were involved as an operations and training instructor.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Well, when I assumed that post until the end of December 1991, my commander was Dragan Petrusic and in 1991 when the elections were won Zijad Caber became the commander. And from that time on until the beginning of the war Zijad Caber was the commander of the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who the commanders were until the end of 1992 before you left to perform other duties.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: I think from the beginning of June the commander was Haso Ribo. And he remained the commander until around the 15th of November, 1992. Then Ahmed Kulanovic took over and I moved to the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of April according to the evidence we have, the presidency took a decision on renaming the BH TO staff and it was supposed to become the Republican TO staff. Tell me whether the municipal staff of Territorial Defence in Travnik accepted the Territorial Defence staff as a legitimate superior command.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: We then received from the district command from the Territorial Defence in Zenica instructions according to which we should pledge our loyalty to that newly formed staff of the Territorial Defence in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. We were to sign a document pledging our loyalty, and this is what we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Given this new situation, the wartime situation, as a result of the attack of the JNA and the Serbian forces launched against Bosnia and Herzegovina, could you tell me whether the Territorial Defence staff in Travnik was able to mobilise men in accordance with a previously drafted mobilisation plan, and if this was not the case, could you explain to us why it was not possible to do this.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The TO municipal staff in the earlier period just before the war developed so-called tactical units which were supposed to be used for combat operation territory of Travnik municipality. These units were replenished in accordance with or on the basis of the national composition of the population. Likewise, area units, local commune units, were also brought up to strength on the basis of the national composition of the population. On the 8th of April, the situation was such that these plans were quite simply not valid. They had to be cancelled and we had to start from zero because the Serbian population, the majority of the Serbian population, had already moved to a territory where the inhabitants were mainly Serbs because they had joined the former JNA which, under the pretext of carrying out military manoeuvres, had taken quite a bit of the Travnik municipality, the Vlasic plateau, the Prijedor area. So these units couldn't be mobilised like this. And similarly, in addition to the Serbian population, the Croatian population didn't join these TO units but they organised themselves on a national basis. So this is something that happened at the same staff. There was the TO staff in the municipality, but an HVO headquarters started functioning in the area of Travnik municipality at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to men liable for municipality service who according to wartime plans were supposed to join JNA units?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Perhaps I haven't explained this sufficiently. In the municipality of Travnik it appeared as if things had been prepared in advance, because when I started working in the municipality of Travnik there were two brigades from the JNA reserve force. But before 1991, both brigades were disbanded. The JNA units in the municipality of Travnik barely existed because new brigades were formed, the 19th in Donji Vakuf was formed. The 22nd in Skender Vakuf was formed too. They provided them with equipment that had been brought in from Slovenia and Croatia. This was equipment kept in the warehouse in Slimena. There were a lot of men who hadn't been given assignments. They were wandering aimlessly. Quite simply, they didn't fit in with the mobilisation plans that the TO had drafted.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You have just given us a fairly clear explanation of the situation as far as men are concerned and so as the possibility of mobilising them is concerned, since the mobilisation plans you had prepared were more or less invalid. Now, could you please tell me what happened to the Territorial Defence's weapons, and as you said, the Territorial Defence staff had placed itself under the control of the Yugoslav army as early as 1991.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: In Travnik at that time in 1991, there was a JNA barracks, a small barracks and a technical battalion was located there. But what is important is under the pretext of carrying out military manoeuvres in 1991 and in the beginning of 1992, the Komar area was taken by JNA units. This is on the road N5 which goes through Travnik towards Bosanska Krajina. They also took over the entire Vlasic area as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please point to these areas on the model we have, if that is possible.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: As I said, this is the road that connects Travnik by the Lasva valley in Bosna in the direction of Sarajevo. It connects Travnik and Sarajevo. The JNA units had taken this pass from one side of the pass you have the Komar mountain and on the other side you have Radalj. The next area the JNA units took is this plateau called Smet Gostilj. And then they reached the Galice plateau, Devecani, and they approached the radio transmitter on the top Paljenik. If we have a good look you can see from this side there's Travnik and Lasva valley which were under complete blockade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You may go back to your seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll perhaps have our break now and resume at about 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now resume. You may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, you were just telling us that some of the JNA forces were deployed at elevated positions outside of Travnik and practically, totally blocked the town. What happened to the TO weapons under the control of the army? Were they returned to the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence weapons remained in the Slimena warehouse. They were never returned to the TO, whereas the JNA units secured the warehouse, Slimena. When they were leaving they blew up the warehouse. In particular, they blew up the warehouse where weapons and other materiel of the TO in Travnik were located.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Given what you have just said, what sort of weapons did the Territorial Defence staff have when war broke out?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: On the 8th of April when a new TO staff was formed, a new staff of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Travnik didn't have a single gun. First of all, the weapons that the TO staff had in order to distribute the weapons to its members, these weapons were weapons that when leaving the institute in Travnik and the barracks of the JNA in Travnik, these were weapons that would remain in those facilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell how many weapons were concerned and what kind of weapons.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: I wasn't personally present at those two locations, but according to the briefing given by the commander of the Territorial Defence, or rather of the municipal staff at the time there were about a hundred barrels, a hundred long barrels. So these were ordinary army rifles. And I refer to the maintenance depot and the barracks. These were the two facilities.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In such a situation, given that you were no longer able to follow the plan for mobilising men and given that you no longer had any weapons, was there any combat in the area of your municipal staff? Who confronted the enemy?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: In the area of the municipal staff of Travnik the first combat, or rather the attack launched by the Serbian army against the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was carried out on the 20th of April, 1992, in the Turbe area, that is to say from the direction of Komar and Radalj. And the Serbian forces attacked Turbe, whereas the defenders of Turbe were local people. There was the Turbe police station and only the police station had weapons and was able to resist, whereas the locals of Turbe had their own weapons which they had obtained on the black market or they had hunting weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: With regard to the attack of the Serbian forces against Travnik and with regard to the lines that the TO and other armed forces had established, could you show us the location of these lines on the map and on the model.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Could I just clarify your question. Do you mean on that very day or are you referring to the line -- the front line, or the first line that was established in the municipality of Travnik?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I think it would be important for you to tell us about the direction from which the attack was launched and where was that first line, the front line, that was established after the initial combat operations.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Before I get up to show this on the map to you or to draw it, in the Travnik municipality after Turbe there was fighting on the Vlasic plateau and lines were established both in Turbe and throughout the territory of the municipality of Travnik. This is why I asked you whether I should draw the lines after the beginning of those combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You don't have to do so at this moment, but please could you point to those lines on Vlasic or rather Turbe, as you just said. Could you show us where those lines were, how far they were from various places and from the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Here we have Turbe. The first attack of the Serbs and Montenegrins was carried out from the direction of Radalj, as I said. They attacked Turbe, an inhabited place which is where the Turbe police station was located. Some of the inhabitants -- the attack was launched from the Vocnijak [phoen] village. And in the pretext of doing work on the water supply -- that's what they said, because the TO staff had a warehouse in Turbe and a training centre for its men. They told us that they were digging canals for the water supply but they were preparing defence lines. The attack was from Vocnijak against Turbe. And along 9 the Lasva Valley, that's where a defence line was established. The Serbian 10 forces immediately took “Metalorad”, the metal works which was in the middle, 11 in an area between the Territorial Defence and Serb forces. The Serbian forces then took this entire Radalj area. They took Vasici Kuca, elevated points in Komar towards Karaula. This valley here is the valley of Karaula. And our forces facing them mounted some sort of defence to repel the attack launched by these forces. Then on the other side, on this road in the direction of Komar, the Serbian forces held this entire road and they then moved over to the other side and held this area which is called Sarmaja. Lines were established in the village of Goles the inhabitants of which were mixed. Half of them were Serbs and the other half were Bosniaks. In Goles itself, in the village, that's were lines were established. As for Komar and elevated points, these areas were held by the Serbian forces. As far as the other area is concerned, this territory here -- well, there is a part missing on the map, but this part is called Smet, and we have Gostilj. So it's above the Karaula valley. Karaula is at an altitude of about 600 metres and the altitude of Smet and Gostilj is about 1.000 or 1.100 metres. There were tanks and other equipment with which they arrived in this area and they took this entire Karaula valley. On the other side as I said a minute ago, there is part of this place called Galice. They took that, and if you have a look at the map you will see how much higher it is in relation to the Turbe valley. They reached Devecani and took Devecani. On the 1st of May, 1992, they carried out a frontal attack and used all their equipment and all their forces and they took the radio transmitter on Paljenik, which the Travnik police force was guarding. They were from Han Bila. In this attack there were strong Serbian and Montenegrin forces that captured a significant of our soldiers and the line was established along this road which leads to Paljenik. And then it was established beyond the Cavo feature which is 1817 metres, Pavo 1807 metres. Then we have Crni Vrh, which was also taken. Then there's Kraljevo Guvno, Tvrda Ravan, Duge; they didn't take Ljuta Greda but they took Duge Kvrkusa. And then via Bijelik they established a line in the direction of Neokrnje at the border of the municipality of Travnik with Teslic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just briefly could you indicate these lines on the model. It won't be necessary to provide any additional explanations to the elevations and villages that they took.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Here you can see Turbe. The attack came from Radalj. They came all the way down to Turbe and it was in Turbe that a line was established. On the other side -- I said they crossed to the other side of the road and took possession of these elevated points here alongside the line between parts of the villages -- part of the village of Goles. The line went through Goles, the line between TO and Serb forces. I'm not talking about Radalj because the whole area was taken possession of, including elevated points. Karaulska valley. In this area it was Smet Gostilj and the road leading to Skender Vakuf and Banja Luka was taken possession of. They controlled the area of Galice, this part here. Then they went over to this other area of Galice and the relay at the highest point of Vlasic, 1.903 metres included Cavo, Pavo and all the way to Crni Vrh. They took all these points here, which are all located in the Travnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated. Could you please tell us, in light of this very dispersed structure and the possibilities of mobilising the population in case of war, what were the measures that were taken by the Territorial Defence to mobilise the population? What parameters were taken into account? According to what structure was it done and at what pace?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Upon the call-up for the volunteers to report to the Territorial Defence staffs, the municipal staff recorded such volunteers. They were not yet ready to establish proper units. The TO wanted to put under control, pursuant to an order issued by the superior command, what was already in the area, in the field. So what we could do was to tour the area, inspect the existing village units, and proceed with organising them into proper units. Pursuant to the principles which were applicable in the former Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, the replenishment of JNA was supposed to be done by the secretariat of National Defence. However, in this situation this was not done. Or rather, people were dispatched to the area, into the field, in order to inspect the situation in particular villages and to draw lists of potential candidates so that the Territorial Defence staff could then register them as potential members of such units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to these purely military difficulties that you were faced with, what was the situation in Travnik which affected the preparation of the defence and the establishment of the units?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: As early as April 1992, from the villages of the Vlasic area such as Mudrik, Vitoljevi, Sazici, Mehici - these are all Bosniak villages - inhabitants were expelled from these villages. So we had refugees from these villages and villagers had already started coming up from Bosanska Krajina. However, we as a military component -- of course this had a certain influence on us, however the greatest problem for us was the fact that in parallel with the municipal Territorial Defence staff, we had -- or rather, all of a sudden there appeared another military organisation that wanted to implement the decision of the presidency of the BH on placing all armed groups and individuals under the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What parallel structure are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Well, there is the municipality staff of the HVO, and Croatian population joined the HVO forces that were established within the HVO staff, municipal HVO staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Were there any other armed groups in addition to HVO which refused the command of the municipal staff, the control and command of the municipal staff?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: There were members of HOS at the time. There were units or groups made up of Croatian nationals, although later there were Bosniaks as well in these HOS units. In addition to that, all kinds of self-organised groups passed through Travnik. And I think that later I noticed something which was rather odd for our area, the fact that these people shouted out "Tekbir" and things like that, people who were not members of the Territorial Defence of the Travnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said that a parallel command, HVO, was established at one point in time and then you went on to enumerate a number of other groups. This HVO staff and HVO units, did they have any military characteristics at the time? Were they similar to military formations, or are we only talking about individuals and individual groups?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The commander of the HVO staff in Travnik at the beginning was Ivica Stojak. Ivica Stojak was a commander of a part of an antisabotage unit. So it was one of the detachments that had to respond to the TO mobilisation call-up. At the time,I would meet him from time to time. He would come to see the commander. We talked a number of times. And what we were able to conclude is that he was tasked with establishing an HVO staff, but he was saying, or rather they were saying that the objective was common objective and that was the defence against the Serbian aggressor. However, there was not enough interest or perhaps not enough willingness on his part - or perhaps he was never given consent for that - to establish a joint unified command so that we could establish proper joint armed forces which would have been much easier and much better for the defence against the enemy. If I may just add one point. A moment ago just before we broke, when I stood up to indicate something on the map I was able to hear the interpreter in my earphones. However, now I cannot hear the interpretation and that's why I don't know whether they have finished or not. So I am trying to make -- to pause because you warned me to do so. However I'm not able to respect that completely because I don't hear the interpretation at all times. Is it possible perhaps to increase the volume of the interpretation so that I can tell when they have finished?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your kind permission, Mr. President, I would like to ask the assistance of the usher. Perhaps the usher could check whether it is possible for the witness to hear the interpretation in his earphones so that he has enough time to wait before he answers my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please. Please continue and then we will be able to see if there is any problem with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, like I told you at the beginning, maybe I don't hear very well. But perhaps I can continue without really hearing the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as interpretation is concerned, you don't need interpretation because you speak the same language. Perhaps you don't need earphones at all. But perhaps it would be a good idea for the witness to follow on the screen the interpretation. In that way, he will not need earphones, which he doesn't need because he speaks the same language, except if the Chamber asks a question either in English or in French. But if it's only you asking the questions, I don't think the witness needs earphones. Unless you don't hear the counsel. But the counsel can then shout if you cannot hear her very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear the counsel and I think I can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, the commander of the HVO staff did not accept the command of the municipal staff. Is that what you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why is it that the municipal staff failed to take any measures, including military measures, to place the HVO units under its control, under its command, in light of the fact that they constituted legitimate force of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The municipal staff of the Territorial Defence at that time did not have a mandate to that effect. They were not able to make such decisions. No soldier could reach such a decision. Such a decision could only be reached at a political, higher, level. But apart from that the HVO, such as it was, was useful for the purposes of the defence against the enemy because they did maintain certain portions of the line against the Serbian aggressor. So of course anyone taking part in the defence was more than welcome. But it was not up to us. We couldn't reach a decision of that kind, and that was not the situation prevailing in the Travnik municipality area only. It was a much greater, larger problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about the organisation of the municipal staff in peacetime. We are in 1992 now. Had there been any changes in terms of rules and regulations and the position of the Territorial Defence staff in the overall system of the state?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Right after the order was issued to that effect, we started establishing units and staffs similar to the ones we had had before. That is to say, it was our objective to establish such units in all inhabited areas and we wanted to include everyone in the defence. Now, the immediate threat of war had been declared; not war, not wartime. So it was not possible to involve the entire population. It had to be done on a voluntary basis, and that is how those units were established. However, changes were taking place rapidly and regulations had changed for the Territorial Defence. A new staff had been established, a new staff at the level of the republic. And it was at that level that appropriate regulations were adopted. So it was in accordance with that that we acted in the field on our terrain. We reorganised units and took certain measures in response and pursuant to the regulations that had been adopted in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were a member of the Territorial Defence staff in spring and summer of 1992. As such, were you aware of the fact that regulations from the area of defence had been adopted? And if so, what was the link of these regulations with the formal regulations on the All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: At the beginning of the war we implemented the rules and regulations 2 of the former Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that is the law that had applied to the armed forces including Territorial Defence in the former Yugoslavia. I don't know exactly when that was, but at one point these laws were declared null and void and new decrees, presidential decrees were adopted, including the decrees on national defence and armed forces. So we endeavoured to behave in the spirit of these regulations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Tell us please, at that time were you aware of the aims and objectives of these decrees adopted at the level of the state? And if so, tell us which specific decree provided for the aims and objectives of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The units of the Territorial Defence received at the municipal level the platform of the presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina on activity in wartime. And that platform, so-called platform, was welcome and approved of because it implied a multi-ethnic state, a kind of state that we were fighting for. However, members of the Territorial Defence also recognise their possibility to find a peaceful solution for the current problems, for the existing problems. So yes, we did receive such a decree. We gave it appropriate interpretation, and this particular act was welcome in the Travnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said a moment ago that HVO was established at one point in time. In the Travnik municipality on the part of the Territorial Defence staff, were any efforts made with the objectives of having a joint command and coming up with a joint plan for fighting the enemy? And if Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. yes, can you please tell us what the results were of such efforts.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: As I already indicated, at the first multi-party elections, SDA and HDZ won the majority of votes. Both of these parties spent considerable time negotiating. I don't know what it was that they discussed. However, the results of their talks were -- first of all, when HVO staff, when a commander of the HVO did not express interest to come under a joint command, then there were attempts to reach a common solution for fighting the common enemy. I know that because the late Stojak would come from time to time to the TO staff. Whether he talked to the commander, I don't know. I talked to him as well because we had known each other from before. The next step in these negotiations was to establish a joint staff, a joint staff of armed forces of the Travnik municipality. So it was no longer Territorial Defence staff -- the idea was that it would no longer be the Territorial Defence staff, because as far as Croats were concerned the expression "Territorial Defence" was not really appreciated. They thought of it as a Serbian expression. So we wanted to avoid it. And we came up with the proposal of having armed forces staff. And the idea was that the HVO, HDZ, and SDA would delegate their participants, their members, into this armed forces staff. However, this idea was never implemented. Who knows? Many casualties could have perhaps been avoided, but such an agreement never came to life.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Because of the fact that there had already been an HVO staff and because the Croat community, the Croat leadership, had already decided to establish an armed force of their own. And they already had decided that they would not recognise any other force. Territorial Defence was a legitimate organ and the decisions of the Territorial Defence, they thought, were not legitimate. And they also thought that the Territorial Defence forces should be subordinate to HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was proclaimed at one point that you were fighting a common enemy. I would like to know where the HVO lines against the common enemy - that is, the Serb forces - were being established.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: I would like to point out a very good example, and that is the village of Turbe, inhabited by Croats, Serbs, and Bosniaks. Bosniaks and Croats did manage to organise common defence in that village. I'm saying this because a moment ago when I spoke about the defence of Turbe - and because this is the first time I find myself in this situation. Maybe I omitted to say that but now I'm correcting myself. The Croat community of Turbe did take active part in defence. And for quite some time they were engaged with Armija with the defence against the enemy. So the Territorial Defence worked together with the members of the Croatian community in Turbe. As for other parts of the theatre, other parts of the front line, my experience is mostly negative because I did tour those lines at the time. I'm afraid I'm sometimes confusing these terms because the situation was rather complex. In the area west of Travnik and south of Turbe -- that is, in Bijelo, Buca, Pula, Dolac -- there was a line which was maintained by the army of BH. And in the area of Mescema two kilometres away from that the line was manned by the HVO. So the front line was manned by the BH army and the HVO maintained the rear line. Another example is the Vlasic plateau. The second-highest point is Vlaska Gromila, 1.919 or 20 metres. That is where the Armija was. Whereas the HVO manned or was deployed on the positions in the area of Krunovo. I can perhaps indicate on the map or the model. But again it was on the depth of the area. Again, it was not the front line that the HVO manned. And if I may add, the HVO manned the line in those areas inhabited by Croatian population --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am beginning to be concerned. You have scheduled this witness for six hours. We have now spent two hours talking about defence, operations, the issue of Serbs. And on list number 52 you said that the witness would be examined on the issue of municipalities; where the events took place; about the role of the 306th Brigade; the issue of Mujahedin and so on. I fear that if we continue on this pace we will not be able to finish his testimony in two days. I strongly appeal to you to finish these questions concerning Serbs and Turbe and focus what is really important in the testimony of this witness. Otherwise we will never finish. We still have three-quarters of an hour before the break and then again one hour and that will be one-half of your testimony. Tomorrow we have to think of the cross-examination and also the questions of the Judges. So I really strongly appeal to you to focus on the essential.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. These questions are somewhat longer because these are our first witnesses. I only have a few things before I move to the 306th Brigade. And with your indulgence, I would like to finish these questions so that I can move to the next subject, that is the position of Mr. Siljak in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In connection with what you have told us so far, witness, tell us please: In Travnik where the municipal staff of the defence is located, who is the authority? Who is the local authority there?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: In Travnik, it was the War Presidency of the municipality of Travnik acting as Municipal Assembly of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, did the municipal staff at any point in time have any superior position with respect to this civilian organ of government, that is, the War Presidency, which acted as Municipal Assembly at the time?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: None whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In Travnik town, were there any other organs which had their military, armed wing, and did Territorial Defence at the time have any superior position with respect to them?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: In addition to the Territorial Defence, I believe I indicated at the beginning that members of the MUP were the first ones who were armed. There was a police station in Travnik and there was a network of police stations in the municipality, and their members were armed. And they were in direct communication with the public security services centre in Zenica. And as organs of the Travnik municipality, they were subordinate to the War Presidency. They were never subordinate to the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, the municipality of Travnik or the War Presidency, did they have any responsibilities with respect to TO units as armed forces in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: According to the earlier law on defence, the Travnik Municipal Assembly or any other municipal assembly decided about the mobilisation of units, about the needs of units. It took care of equipping units. And as I said, they funded the training. And similarly, during this period they continued to proceed in this manner because the commander of the TO, the second one, Ribo Haso, was appointed by the War Presidency. And later the War Presidency also appointed instead of Ribo Haso, Kulenovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we have provided the Chamber with enough information about the organs in Travnik in 1992. I would like to ask the following: At any point in time did you notice that foreigners were appearing in Travnik? Foreigners who were not refugees, who would arrive from Krajina or from occupied territory.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: As I said I performed the duties for assistant for operational and training matters, and those duties consisted of evaluating the situation and suggesting what action could be taken to the commander. That's why I was often in the field but when returning from the field I noticed the presence of such foreigners. Some of them were in civilian clothing and I don't know whether they were members of humanitarian organisations. There were journalists who were present, too. I'm not sure which countries they were from but I did notice their presence there.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the municipal staff did you at any point in time in 1992, did you accept these foreigners as integral parts of TO units and did you have any contact with them? Did you provide them with logistical support? Did you provide them with weapons and the like?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: On the premises of the municipal staff, I never saw them. As I said, I spent most of my time in the field. But as to whether they were in those units or whether they were some kind of unit, I would have [Realtime transcript read in error: "wouldn't"] know that. Since I was the assistant commander for operational and training matters, if any operation was being planned I was to be informed about it. I was to make suggestions as to how forces should be used and I was to draft plans. So we didn't have any such foreigners and we didn't provide them with any logistical support either.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: On page 43, line 10, my colleague has just pointed out that the transcript says that he wouldn't know that, whereas he said "I would know that." If they had participated, I would have been aware of the fact. So could that part of the transcript please be corrected. Mr. Siljak, towards the end of 1992, can you tell me whether there were any significant organisational changes within the BH army, and if you are familiar with any such changes could you tell us about the nature and could you tell us what sort of a position you were given within the framework of those changes.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: In the municipality of Travnik, given the organisational changes, in the BH republic army, some of the units were built up, as a team of officers came from the republican staff who supervised the changes -- the organisational changes in Travnik municipality. The order was that in Travnik municipality the 17th Krajina Brigade should first be formed. It was composed of refugees from Bosanska Krajina. There were hundreds of thousands of them who had passed through Travnik from the 1st Krajina Battalion and the 7th Krajina Brigade who used to be in the municipality of Travnik. From these units, the 17th Krajina Brigade was formed. And from the able-bodied men or from the units that were present in the municipality of Travnik, in the Territorial Defence defence they formed the 312th Motorised Brigade, from the detachment in the Lasva valley. And the 306th Brigade was to be formed from the detachment in the Bila valley. You asked me about the position I was given then. I was appointed as the chief of staff of the 306th Brigade, since I knew the territory, I knew the men, I knew the settlements in that part of Travnik municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who became the commander of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Esid Sipic was appointed as the commander of that brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you immediately assume those duties?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: No, not immediately, because at that time in the territory of Travnik, General Praljac was present as a representative of the Croatian president Tudjman and Jasmin Jaganjac was also there as a representative of President Izetbegovic. Their tasks were to form a joint command which would contribute to calming the situation and solving the problems in Travnik in the month of October, then they were to plan joint action against the Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor. Within that command my role was that of an operations officer. My task at the time was a task I was assigned by Jasmin Jaganjac. On the map of the territory of Novi Travnik and Travnik, I was to indicate all the forces of the BH army, all the artillery that was available. And the HVO operations officers were supposed to do the same. I performed that task. I didn't go to assist with the formation of the 306th Brigade. I was involved in that work. But since the HVO didn't do its part of the task, I didn't continue. I was sent to the 306th to continue working on the formation of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, let's move on to the formation of the 306th Brigade now and everything that happened in the territory covered by the 306th Brigade. Could you please tell me now, what was the composition of the population? And which TO units entered the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: In the area of the Bila Valley they had already formed TO detachments. The Han Bila detachment had been formed, and that covered the villages of Han Bila, Cukle, Pode, Brajkovici, Jake, Alihodze, Karahodze, Zolote and Rajici. The able-bodied men from those villages were those who formed that detachment. The 2nd Detachment was the Mehurici one, which was composed of men from Mehurici, Jezerci, Orahovo, Fazlici, and Boljavje [phoen]. Then there was the Ljuta Greda detachment composed of able-bodied men from the villages of Suhi Dol, Dub and Visnjevo. The detachment had previously been formed and it covered the villages of Krpeljici, Mosor, Radojcici, Bandol, and Vukovine and Maline.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Siljak. Perhaps it's not necessary to mention each village. I think you mentioned them a while ago and you have now told us that there were detachments and the 306th was formed out of the population in -- out of the men in those detachments. Could you tell me, when the brigade itself was being formed, were there any problems as far as the formation and establishment of this brigade is concerned? And to what extent did these problems effect establishing this brigade in a normal manner?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Well, with regard to the first orders about forming the 306th Brigade, these orders stipulated that all other detachments and all the units including the Patriotic League Battalion that had previously been formed, the Sipliske battalion that had been formed it was said that they should enter the 306th Brigade. The commander of the Patriotic League Battalion did not want such an order to be carried out because he wanted to enter the 314th Motorised Brigade. And his relative was supposed to be appointed commander of that brigade. That's when the first problems arose. We lost quite a lot of time on this before we managed to clarify the situation, and finally that battalion did enter the 304th Motorised Brigade. It became part of it. But I'd also like to say that the men from that battalion were men from Gluha Bukovic, Zagradje, and Skomorje, these villages. They were from the territory of the municipality Travnik, or rather the territory of the Bila Valley.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: If I have understood you correctly, the inhabitants of the Bila valley did not all join the 306th Brigade. I apologise if this question is leading. If it is correct, could you please tell me who from that territory mobilised the inhabitants in the Bila Valley.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Well, the able-bodied men, most of them were in the 306th Brigade. But one battalion from the villages I have mentioned entered the 314th Zenica Brigade. And then there was a Howitzer battery of the 312th brigade. And then some of the inhabitants on their own initiative were included into the 7th Muslim Brigade. So from the area of the Bila Valley able-bodied men entered various units. So the 306th Brigade couldn't be brought up to strength in accordance with the usual standards.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will now ask the usher to show the witness a series of documents to see whether the witness has anything to say about them. We've already provided these documents to the Chamber, to the registrar, and to our colleagues from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, could you please have a look at the documents. Under the titles "formation of the 306th Mountain Brigade," have a look under numbers 2, 3, 4, and 5. And first of all, could you tell me whether you recognise these documents. Documents 2, 3, 4, and 5.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Document number 2 refers to the problem that we had in relation to the Patriotic League and battalion. It says that they will be entering the 314th, that they -- that it won't enter the 306th Brigade, it won't become part of the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Document number 3.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: It also states exactly which units will enter from the Mehurici Detachment. It mentions which units will enter the 314th Motorised Brigade because there were several problems and it was necessary for the 3rd Corps command to intervene on several occasions to solve the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at document number 4 dated the 20th of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: This was a reaction to these events.

utterances.speaker: MS. BENJAMIN
utterances.text: Chamber's indulgence please. I think the Prosecution is a little lost here. Because it says 1, 2, and 3, 157/10. We can't find 157/10 because we have it in 015 going those numbers. So I would have to go through the whole pile to be able to determine the dates you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I was just showing the witness the documents in the order that they have been placed in. But perhaps there is some confusion because I didn't indicate the numbers from the lists which have been provided as defence numbers. The first document that the witness commented on is dated the 6th of December, 1992, and the number is 0515; that's the Defence number. The second document is a document dated the 4th of December, 1992. The number of this document is Defence number 0526. The third document which the witness is commenting on right now is dated the 20th of December, 1992; the number of this document is 0531. All these documents are referred to on our list under numbers 2, 3, and 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Chamber is following you. There aren't any problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, you started commenting on this document dated the 20th of December, 1992, which is addressed to the command of the 306th Brigade, it's from Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: Authorisation for the battalion of the Patriotic League to enter the 314th Motorised Brigade gave rise to reactions elsewhere. So the company of the Mehurici local commune directly contacted the command of the 3rd Corps requesting that they too join some other unit or that they be independent. Because their intention, the intention of those units was to hold the defence lines above their villages. So this is a response on an order from the 3rd Corps command saying how this matter should be regulated and stating how units should be formed. It states that a specialist team should do this, and not individuals as they see fit.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Siljak, for how long did you have to confront the problem of forming units and training the soldiers, the men, who were supposed to enter given brigades?

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The formation of the 306th Brigade or just compiling lists for the brigade took almost two months, and this is why. In 1992 in one detachment in over one day in the Okrinje [phoen] region, six men died as a result of a mortar shell and four men were seriously wounded. All these men were from the village of Gluha Bukovica. We wanted to avoid such tragedies. For one single village, this is an immense tragedy. We wanted to have a unit which was not territorial based in the Bila Valley. So we issued a task to the organ for mobilisation and organisation and requested that they compile lists and that they take this into consideration. We did this together with this organ for mobilisation and organisation, so the first battalion that was from areas such as Kotor Varos and Skender Vakuf, they took over the defence line on the 21st of December. But when a second battalion had to go and take over a line facing a Serbian and Montenegrin aggressor, we faced obstructions. Because people didn't want to go there on non-territorial basis, but they wanted the inhabitants of one single village to be in the unit. This is one of the problems we had to confront. There were no one to replace these men. So we again started forming units in order to transform the previous detachments into battalions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As to other problems -- as far as other problems were concerned, where were your men located? The 306th have the facilities for billeting these listed men in barracks.

utterances.speaker: REMZIJA SILJAK
utterances.text: The 306th brigade -- well, first of all I could talk about the commands. They didn't have any facilities for accommodating the commands, but they found facilities in the premises of the Bila mine. We didn't have any barracks anywhere, but the commands of the battalions usually used schools as premises, the schools that were in that area. So the 1st Battalion command was located in the school in Mehurici. The 2nd Battalion command was located in Peljici. There isn't a school there. They were in a cell or a garage. That's where the communications centre was. And the command was located in a public utilities premises of the local commune, which was very small. The 3rd battalion command was located in a school in Han Bila and the 4th Battalion command was located in the school in Visnjevo.
